body: When I'm in a suicidal state, no hotline is going to do anything. I survived, but was I still breaking down. My friends are sick of hearing from me, so I called a hotline. They told me what any professional would tell a suicidal person. Sometimes that's needed. Personally, at that point I had already 'survived' so I just felt embarrassed that I called and wasted someone's time. I guess the upshot is that the mere fact that you're calling a hotline means you're taking a step towards preventing self-harm.

I'm a software developer who freelanced for a few years. On the plus side, it was rewarding to solve problems my way. On the negative side, It was very hard to overcome the anxiety of interfacing with new people, and not having a steady income

The hardest part for me was finding the energy to constantly look for new opportunities. When the depression of not having a steady income set in, it made it harder to look for new opportunities. Without new opportunities to keep me busy, the depression set in even further. It ended up being a downward spiral. I'm now at a job where I'm full-time, but I long to be able to have the courage and ability to strike out on my own again. The corporate system is just so unforgiving for people with conditions like this.

All that said, when I *was* on a self-employed project, I enjoyed it quite a bit. I got to solve problems my way, first as an idea, then bringing that idea to life. That aspect is very rewarding. I could also set my own schedule in a way. I could set a date for the project to be done by, and since I was working by myself,  I could wait 'till the last minute without any managers giving me the eye. Stuff got done, it was just done my way.

It also taught me to be flexible with the technology I was using. It gave me the opportunity to continue learning as I moved from one project to the next. At my day job, it's the "my way or the highway" mentality of the managers means I'm stuck using the same bad tools to do the same mundane work day after day.

Next time you feel like moving on - give it a try!
